structure_proposals.why: Legs A gives the front of your leg nine sets — leg press, split squats and extensions — against three of leg curl and no hinge at all, and on 2 August all three of those curl sets finished at the top of the range at 135 for fifteen, fifteen and fifteen, so this makes it four; the card below takes that same set off Legs B, so your week's hamstring total does not move.

You asked in writing on 16 August whether four sets of leg curls on the same day as your RDLs is too many hamstrings — Legs B is the one day you hinge, and it is the only leg day carrying both, so this is that fourth set moving to Legs A rather than disappearing, and your weekly curl volume stays at seven.

On all three Legs A nights your first leg-press set has been a build-up — 160, 160 and 180 against top sets of 220, 220 and 240 — so the four sets the plan asks for are really three of work plus a ramp, and at three minutes of rest each this is the most expensive slot on your longest session; three sets prices it as what it already is, and with the leg-curl set added above the night stays the same length.
